item.title: bro i had a disappointing ass dinner. the server kept hyping us up abt how the food uses so many spices therefore it's super flavorful. Tell me WHERE were the spices when i got my entree because that shit was BLAND AS FUCK & the whole appeal of the restaurant was that it's supposed to be flavorful moroccan cuisine. is the flavor in the room with us because it must still be in morocco. have you had a similar experience recently?? What would you do in this situation??
item.description:
4.2.26 2:25 am
Q: bro i had a disappointing ass dinner. the server kept hyping us up abt how the food uses so many spices therefore it's super flavorful. Tell me WHERE were the spices when i got my entree because that shit was BLAND AS FUCK & the whole appeal of the restaurant was that it's supposed to be flavorful moroccan cuisine. is the flavor in the room with us because it must still be in morocco. have you had a similar experience recently?? What would you do in this situation??
A: there is something particularly humorous about something being hyped way up and then actually being the opposite of what it's hyped to be. this reminds me many many years ago at burger thing, when they first introduced the "chicken fries" (or maybe one of the many times the re-introduced them), they come in a tall, top-heavy box. the box is somehow designed so it has a sauce holder on top. a little slot where you can put the sauce container. They had arrows pointing to it and then had a description "Sauce goes here. Yup, we promoted the guy who invented it." whether or not they actually promoted someone, i dont know or care, but here's the thing: the sauce fits fine in the slot, but as soon as you start taking the fries out, to eat them, the box immediately falls over. it only works when the box is full of chicken fries. this brilliant invention immediately fails as soon as you start using it. What would have seemed mildly silly, became an even more humorous spectacle based on the hype story written on the box. i'm also thinking of debut of the tesla cybertruck, where they demonstrated the unbreakable windows by hitting it with a sledge hammer and the window immediately broke "what you do in this situation" is you collect stories like this for amusement

item.title: you know what always fascinated me? how chord inversions can sometimes completely change the feel despite it still being the same chord...
item.description:
4.2.26 6:09 am
Q: you know what always fascinated me? how chord inversions can sometimes completely change the feel despite it still being the same chord...
A: i mean it's like whether you put the cow on the right side of the barn or the left, in your farm picture. but i think in time you will stop calling them 'inversions' because there is really no 'default' order. actually they way they're most often used in music, chances are, will be in a different order from the 'default' order you may have learned. the truth is, if the page says "C", that doesnt say it all. either the writer or arranger or just you the player with good judgement, will have to decide which octaves to play those notes in. To use a woodworking analogy, the more wood you work the better a woodworker you will be, and thus become better at working with wood

A: basically during the creation process (whether it's writing, production, whatever) you basically just have to have a lot of faith. because every good move that gets made feels like it came by total magic. and then in between those magic waves it's dreadful and nothing happens and nothing works. then whoosh in comes the big magic wave and a bunch of great moves are made, etc. A lot of faith is required, to keep yourself from freaking out in between

item.title: Recently I realized that I had forgotten some lessons that I learned many years ago, and that I needed to teach myself those same lessons again. Forgetting those lessons had begun to negatively impact my life. Have you ever had to do something similar? If so, how did you handle it? I was thinking about how to prevent it from happening again - perhaps writing some things down to reference later. But if I did that, I wasn't sure what was important enough to include, or inversely, what didn't need to be written down at all. I wondered if there was a different approach I hadn't thought of.
item.description:
4.3.26 11:22 am
Q: Recently I realized that I had forgotten some lessons that I learned many years ago, and that I needed to teach myself those same lessons again. Forgetting those lessons had begun to negatively impact my life. Have you ever had to do something similar? If so, how did you handle it? I was thinking about how to prevent it from happening again - perhaps writing some things down to reference later. But if I did that, I wasn't sure what was important enough to include, or inversely, what didn't need to be written down at all. I wondered if there was a different approach I hadn't thought of.
A: you can get into this game of organizing all your wisdom and everything you know, but ultimately youre not going to prevent the ebb and flow of different realizations, different mentalities, different strategies, etc. It's nice to write things down and compare notes, but you can't promise yourself to uphold every mindset all the time

item.title: have you watched nirvanna the band the show the movie? if you have, what'd you think of it?
item.description:
4.9.26 7:02 pm
Q: have you watched nirvanna the band the show the movie? if you have, what'd you think of it?
A: these guys have an amazing filmmaking strategy that relies deeply on improv and editing, and then assembling it into a coherent story in a way that in always feels like a magic trick, keeping you wondering which came first, the writing or the action (and sometimes the answer is not what you think). Unfortunately what starts to ruin this wonderful game is the encroachment of ai. not the use of ai per se, but the encroaching thought of "they could/should have" used it, starts to ruin the amazing game that this team has with their filmmaking method. also one of the strongest points about the nirvanna-the-band content is that the piano playing always matches, and it's actually quite tragic to see jay's hands not matching the sound, giving first time viewers the impression that this is just another movie with a non-piano player playing the piano, which of course it's not. it seems clear to me that what happened is he's probably playing back to the future stuff but they couldnt clear it. so that is a major unfortunate weakness of the movie. generally it's quite strong, perhaps about as strong as the viceland series

item.title: This morning I had a dream that mocked my aspirations for self improvement and progress. I think what it is, is I've grown too accustomed to disappointment. I'm afraid to go after the things I really love. Really want. Ironically it's precisely chasing after these things that would propel me out of the mud now hardened cement. Why am I allowing my nightmares to prove themselves right? item.title: In 987 there is an incredible moment. "Your home was never like that" the chords you go to on "like that" are so beautiful and I really didn't expect them at all. Within the musical context of that part of the song how did you choose to use those chords? I never would've thought of that and would really appreciate some wisedom. Thank you Bill. Huge fan.
item.description:
4.10.26 11:37 pm
Q: In 987 there is an incredible moment. "Your home was never like that" the chords you go to on "like that" are so beautiful and I really didn't expect them at all. Within the musical context of that part of the song how did you choose to use those chords? I never would've thought of that and would really appreciate some wisedom. Thank you Bill. Huge fan.
A: i think it's just a lot of experience doing songs with chords. it's not really that different from what it does at the end of the other similar parts, but it's maybe the equivalent of a behind the back throw. Honestly what that part sounds like to me is, i was feeling stuck in that same melody and basically just repetitions of that same section, and i was feeling restless, so i was getting 'differenty' with the chords to try to compensate. but really i probably would have been more satisfied if i had taken it in a whole different direction there somehow rather than just fitting more stanzas into the same box of a B section earlier established. in fact i feel very similarly about this as to a line that was brought up just the other day, in slow down, where i was also surely feeling restless and dissatisfied with just piling additional stanzas onto the same A and B sections round and round. in both cases the writing was crunched for time on a self imposed emergency schedule as a last resort attempt to save myself from myself

Or perhaps youre asking what's the first thing i do to come up with new ideas for songs. but that's almost never the same time that i go ahead and produce or even finish writing that song. perhaps it should be, but it's not. i go guerilla with my new idea writing, then i go guerilla with middle writing, then from there as soon as i finish a video/song, i already know i'm gonna do another one, that's not a question. the question is which one am i gonna do, and if the writing's not finished then my next question is ok how does it go so far, and then i try to imagine what the next part goes like

item.title: What's going on in the everybody wants to rule the world drum part?
item.description:
4.12.26 6:26 pm
Q: What's going on in the everybody wants to rule the world drum part?
A: you have a triplet feel (you can say it's 4/4 with triplets, or you can say it's 12/8 with eight notes, or even 6/8 depending on how big you want the bars to be on paper), you have 4-on-the-floor, which means the kick drum is hitting all 4 beats, you have snare on 2 and 4 ('backbeat'), and then perhaps what you want to know most is the percussion, there is a percussion accent happening on alternating triplets. which makes a cool pattern when you accent one out of every 2 notes when the notes are grouped in groups of 3. so if you're counting "1 trip let 2 trip let 3 trip let 4 trip let", the percussion accents (the louder notes in the tambourine or shaker or whatever) will occur on "one TRIP let TWO trip LET three TRIP let FOUR trip LET". at least this is what i recall happening. i havent really listened to the song since i saw it in the credits for marty surpreme in the cinema, but the song has been around for decades and i've heard it plenty, and to my best recollection that is what the drums and perc are doing. and the snare will give you some nice fills at the end of the 8 or 16 bar segments, usually "BAP BAP _ BAP BAP BAP" in the last two beats (or the last 6 subdivisions). hopefully my language is more or less intelligible to you. i'm trying to be broad in terms of catering the different kinds of musical or mathematical literacy you may be working with

item.title: How do you approach perfectionism? Sometimes I keep working on a song because it just doesn't sound quite right, but I can't quite tell what's wrong with it. I'm trying to teach myself that the unintentional parts of a song, like the parts I didn't really deliberately make that way but just kind of became that way because I couldn't figure them out, are just as uniquely mine, and thus beautiful as anything else I could write. item.description:
4.13.26 3:12 pm
Q: How do you approach perfectionism? Sometimes I keep working on a song because it just doesn't sound quite right, but I can't quite tell what's wrong with it. I'm trying to teach myself that the unintentional parts of a song, like the parts I didn't really deliberately make that way but just kind of became that way because I couldn't figure them out, are just as uniquely mine, and thus beautiful as anything else I could write. Do you have any kind of similar attitude when trying to become happy with a song that you just can't get "perfect"?
A: perfect is poison anyway, but the good news is it doesnt even exit. so it's like imaginary poison. i CERTAINLY would never pursue this imaginary poison on purpose. but i catch myself reflexively going for it by total accident. sort of like a compulsive twitch. and one needs to certainly slap oneself on the wrist here, because it usually is a sign you are suffocating in an ocd spiral leading to nowhere and need to come up for air

item.title: In an interview you expressed distaste for people saying your name again in the middle of talking, then you said "there's nothing wrong with it until you think about it" - can you elaborate on this? I think I know exactly what you mean but want to hear your thoughts on why it's weird/unsettling
item.description:
4.14.26 12:33 am
Q: In an interview you expressed distaste for people saying your name again in the middle of talking, then you said "there's nothing wrong with it until you think about it" - can you elaborate on this? I think I know exactly what you mean but want to hear your thoughts on why it's weird/unsettling
A: it makes them sound like a sales person, like they are selling something. it's just a classic trick that salespeople do, to think they're being more personable but it certainly has the opposite effect. friends dont do this when it's just 1 on 1, especially in the middle of a conversation. the reason it might be used is to distinguish between multiple people. you are in a room with 5 people, youre having a group discussion, you say "so Bob, i wanted to ask about this...." that makes sense, because you are letting the room know which person you are talking to, but in a 1-on-1 conversation this is useless. and people who do it in a 1-on-1 convo immediately sound very sleezy, to me

item.title: how do i get the hang of chord extensions. im pretty familiar with how regular old triad chords get along with each other but i have no intuition of how chord extensions happen
item.description:
4.14.26 8:36 pm
Q: how do i get the hang of chord extensions. im pretty familiar with how regular old triad chords get along with each other but i have no intuition of how chord extensions happen
A: i regret the fact that the 'academic literature' has led you astray. my advice is, pretend you never heard anyone say 'chord extensions'. the thing they are actually referring to is not anything extended. i mean, think of it this way, have you ever heard one of these things in music? if you havent, then why do you think you need it? just because you hear people talking about it? i mean, what are we listening to anyway, music or people talking about music? I will wait patiently until you hear a song and you ask me 'WHOA, WHATS THAT CHORD THERE?' and then i can be like, "it's these notes in order: bass C, and then in mid-range Bb D Eb G", and it's called "C minor 9", that's just what it's called. and then we can debate the logic of the naming convention from there, but if youve never noticed it naturally in music then there's no reason you should really be curious about it, unless you just want to say "chord extension". which you could just start saying now if you really want to

item.title: how exactly does one write lyrics that rhyme while also conveying frustration, confusion, and romantic difficulty (in the sense of "she doesn't know i exist") and still not sounding like a clichéd fuckin cornball? i ask because i want to music but i'm also bad at rhymes because i intentionally avoid them in my speech and have therefore never gotten good at using them
item.description:
4.14.26 9:27 pm
Q: how exactly does one write lyrics that rhyme while also conveying frustration, confusion, and romantic difficulty (in the sense of "she doesn't know i exist") and still not sounding like a clichéd fuckin cornball? i ask because i want to music but i'm also bad at rhymes because i intentionally avoid them in my speech and have therefore never gotten good at using them
A: 1. write while singing the lines at the same time. 2. dont try to rhyme. "How exactly do you grow a round orange"? that's just how they grow. if you start making things up and singing them, actually you'll find that they will be free to be timed in a way where they dont even have to rhyme, because they wont be like "line, line, line, line". you'll just be saying stuff musically. and then from time to time rhymes may happen automatically. i think the world is kinda brainwashed into thinking a certain way about rhymes, or thinking about rhymes at all, in an unhealthy way for songwriting. Including the fact that when it does happen, what sounds the best is actually just when the vowel is the same but the end consonant is different anyway. but youre seriously shooting yourself in the foot if you try to rhyme on purpose. it's a curse for sure

item.title: what is the story of when you made "La de da de da de da de day oh"?
item.description:
4.17.26 11:00 pm
Q: what is the story of when you made "La de da de da de da de day oh"?
A: ok so in 2009 i finally got fed up with the fact that i didnt seem to be writing any songs despite the fact that i felt like i had more than enough skills to be able to do so. so as a last resort i deeply downgraded my standards and just started scribbling garbage on paper. i wrote a beginning about 'i dont have enough time to say the things i want to say' etc, something very much resembling the first verse you'd recognize from that song. (but also not quite the same). that song lived only on paper and also didnt have the 'la de da' chorus, it did something else instead and ended after about a minute and a half. fast foward to 2012 i finally got fed up with how much songwriting i had done without knowing how to organize it or choose which ones to work on. so i built a master list of everything i had, in order of when it was written, and then i started working on each one. the "i dont have enough time" bit came up, and i fixed the verse, and wrote a chorus (the "la de da" chorus that you would recognize). fast forward to 2017, i'd figured out how to finish and produce songs, but i was really fed up with how long it took. i was trying out a 2-week schedule, alternating between song and not-song, always with a video, alternating whether or not i appear on camera in the video. it SEEMED to work ok with a non-song video called 'soap tips', and next would be to do a song video with me appearing in it. i should have known that this would be impossible in 2 weeks but i tried it anyway. on the selection process i landed on the 'la de da' song, which still hadnt been updated since 2012, so it had just 1 verse and chorus written. BUT.... the day after selection, i started doubting the selection. i actually wanted to switch to a different song. then i went to get a haircut and i was thinking about the selection, as thinking about the 'la de da' song again, and then for some reason just at the moment i was getting into the chair, (songwriting loves to work like this) the first 3 lines of the second verse just rammed itself into my head. so with that momentum i figured ok that's the selection, then at home i finished writing the rest. then i recorded it, made the video, etc, and it all took way way way way way way longer than 2 weeks

item.title: i guess im a big fat liar because i like to say i just make art for myself and other people's opinions are whatever but really im horrified by ai because it can convincingly duplicate all the things i pour real emotion into and the only defense i can offer for my own work is "well i actually did put emotion into it" which is true but no one really cares about because the end result is the same to them. any tips on being less of a big fat liar?
item.description:
4.18.26 1:03 am
Q: i guess im a big fat liar because i like to say i just make art for myself and other people's opinions are whatever but really im horrified by ai because it can convincingly duplicate all the things i pour real emotion into and the only defense i can offer for my own work is "well i actually did put emotion into it" which is true but no one really cares about because the end result is the same to them. any tips on being less of a big fat liar?
A: well, this issue can of course be maximum confusing for everyone, at least for now while we get used to it and learn to understand what it is, what it's not, and what it means and doesnt mean. However, it's not nearly as bad as you think, and in some ways it's absolutely wonderful. let me just disect one of your points here: you say no one cares because the end result is the same..... Even if that's true, imagine if the quantity was cranked up to a trillion. whatever becomes overflowingly abundant becomes de-valued. so now no one cares about the fake version either, just because there is SO much of it, it becomes worthless. now, true, also, that that also means that it devalues any kind of thing that SOUNDS LIKE something the machines would cough up, and that may be considered unfortunate for human people who were making.... lets say 'normalish' music before, .... but the effect that this has on everyone is it cultivates a huge thirst for something new and different. whatever it is that the machines cant cough up, that's what will be desired. this has always been true, but now it's accelerated. yes, people will be using the machines in all kinds of ways up down and sideways, in fantastically creative ways (which perhaps older people will not quite understand), and then at the same time there will also be some people that just choose not to use it, and they reap some pretty crazy advantages from NOT using it. in many ways this is analogous to the invention of synths, the invention of drum machines, the invention of SAMPLING ("effortless, he just stole someone elses song and rapped over it!"), PITCH-CORRECTED VOCALS ("but she cant even sing, shes not a real singer" etc), and so on. All these may be horrifying concepts at first, but the advantages are very genuine, AND the benefits of NOT using them are also genuine. AND, also true, the major thing that really truly moves the needle is CONNECTION with audiences. so as long as your audience is human, they are going to care deeply about the human presence in the art. Difficult to prove at times, yes, this may be. but that is also a very fun and interesting game that will become EXTREMELY satisfying to win, for both the artist and the audience. that being said, i will not be using it at all, for the forseeable future. similar to my decision not to use loops, and not to use any pitch correction. this is certainly not to frown on anyone who does, it's just that i have some very interesting skills in terms of songwriting and playing, which can be used very much to my advantage. The key, of course, is to steer it clear of the generic. For weirdo artists like me, for example, it's a license to not be ashamed of being weird and different. If there ever was any pressure to "try to sound commercial" or "try to sound like what's popular", this new technology will SHATTER that bland obligation, better than i think anything else ever could. being a sentient ass human being is a priceless commodity in art, and its value is now thrust to center stage more than it ever has been before, as any and all mechanical aspects are trivialized and removed from the equation. as usual it reminds me of almost every major invention of yester year

item.description:
4.20.26 7:41 pm
Q: i'm a competent drummer but i want to get better at playing bass and guitar. I'm ok at that too, and am working on functional ear training and singing. i'm trying to learn the bass for long long journey. i'm getting it but very hard for me to memorize it all. idk... maybe the answer is in the song title my question is with the whole music universe of things to learn, do you think there are common traps that people learning music fall into? i feel like i can't decide on what and how much time to put into a specific thing to learn anyway, thank you
A: i'm a competent drummer but i want to get better at playing bass and guitar. I'm ok at that too, and am working on functional ear training and singing. i'm trying to learn the bass for long long journey. i'm getting it but very hard for me to memorize it all. idk... maybe the answer is in the song title in this case if youre memorizing then you are DEFINITELY on the wrong track. for example, i have NO IDEA from memory what exactly the bass plays on that song, in terms of exact notes, but i could play it again just fine, and it would be just as good but with different exact notes my question is with the whole music universe of things to learn, do you think there are common traps that people learning music fall into? sure, memorization, for example i feel like i can't decide on what and how much time to put into a specific thing to learn anyway, thank you i am assuming that you are doing this music stuff because you fell in love with music at some point. so that love will guide you to what you want to do. since i told you earlier what NOT to do on bass, i suppose i have to tell you what i think you should do instead..... it's probably a good idea to just start playing the bass along to songs. you can mute the bass track on the song (nowadays you can do this in a million ways, but probably the easiest way is to just play the track through your phone speaker without headphones. poof, no bass!) and play your own bass through amplification so you can hear your bass but not the song's bass. and that's it, you'll figure out what you need to do. the other thing i would suggest is definitely dont choose artists who have a habit of being complicated like me

item.title: So you record all the different parts to your song...but how do you make them sound like one sound? (In the mix) all my parts sounds so seperate, any mixing advice I guess? You're my favourite musician by far. Thanks
item.description:
4.23.26 3:34 am
Q: So you record all the different parts to your song...but how do you make them sound like one sound? (In the mix) all my parts sounds so seperate, any mixing advice I guess? You're my favourite musician by far. Thanks
A: i can probably spill the beans on this one because it's very old technology, probably been around since the 1930s and everyone's been using it ever since, on everything, but especially on radios and broadcasting and in retail stores. it's called "dynamic range compression" and it levels off the volume, making the loud parts quieter and the quiet parts louder. applying this in various ways is basically how you get all your musicians strapped together like they're coming out of the same box. the devil is in the details of course, but for the problem you suggested, 'compressor' is the main device used for this. the only confusing thing is the title. 'compressor' might make you think it has something to do with files or data but it's a totally different thing same name sorry about the confusion in that regard

item.title: hi Bill. In a literature class in high school, there was an assignment to choose a song that meant a lot to you and to analyze it. I chose 'just did a bad thing'. I was wondering what that song means to You? (note: I dont think there is a "right" or "wrong" way to interpret a song; everyone interprets art differently based on their own experiences and I think that's beautiful. But nonetheless, I'm still curious about how much our takes differ)
item.description:
4.25.26 12:41 pm
Q: hi Bill. In a literature class in high school, there was an assignment to choose a song that meant a lot to you and to analyze it. I chose 'just did a bad thing'. I was wondering what that song means to You? (note: I dont think there is a "right" or "wrong" way to interpret a song; everyone interprets art differently based on their own experiences and I think that's beautiful. But nonetheless, I'm still curious about how much our takes differ)
A: the 2 things most memorable to me, which i always say in response to this, are things relating to the selection process, and the production schedule. for the selection process it's my main example of the explicit failure of over thinking. i had it down to about 20 choices for which song to choose, and then one by one i ruled out each one "no, not this one" "no, not this one" "no, not this one" etc, and then i had ruled them all out. so in a fit of rage, i uncancelled all of those semifinalists and on a total whim picked one that was probably my least favorite, on purpose (it only had the first line so far, 'just did a bad thing' and just seemed totally weak and useless, despite the fact that it was a semifinalist.) As soon as i started writing on it, i realized that this was a great choice, because in fact when you have something weak to work with, it ignites the creative engines with more power. and i noticed this within the first 16 bars or so, i said 'wow, i feel more alive now because im forced to compensate for a weak first line'. maybe in fact the 'cancel' line is coming from the fact that the other 'better' songs were cancelled. anyway, the other thing notable for me about this song has to do with the production schedule, because i had recently fallen off the 2 week schedule and was kind of dangling by a thread, in shambles and tears. but it was done in 4 weeks instead of two. which is much quicker than it usually is without a schedule, because i'd just been on the habit of doing it on schedule so i was still relatively quick, but it was slower than a schedule. so sometimes it feels like a 'sweet spot', as i sometimes say, i accidentally worked on it for too long and not long enough, which inadvertantly was maybe just the right amount of time

item.title: how do you learn music so you can think in it like a language? i am too old to a native speaker of it now. do i just learn it like usual with theory first and try express ideas in it and fail and try again until it's serviceable? or would theory be putting the cart before the horse? where the horse is playing an instrument rather than speech and theory is the writing you learn later after the sounds.. is language even an adequate analogy for music or is it far beyond something as limiting as words thank yiu
item.description:
4.26.26 2:40 pm
Q: how do you learn music so you can think in it like a language? i am too old to a native speaker of it now. do i just learn it like usual with theory first and try express ideas in it and fail and try again until it's serviceable? or would theory be putting the cart before the horse? where the horse is playing an instrument rather than speech and theory is the writing you learn later after the sounds.. is language even an adequate analogy for music or is it far beyond something as limiting as words thank yiu
A: the language analogy is of course my standard analogy. if you try to 'study' the mechanics before doing it, it wont make any sense to you. like learning 'grammar', think back to studying english grammar, at, let's say, age 8, for example. was that before you could speak, or after? it was after. if you tried to study english grammar before you could speak, it wouldnt make any sense. and it barely makes any difference on how you speak, because you already know how to use it without knowing you know and the other similarity in general to language learning is (and this may be actually a misconception about both), it's easy to learn but it takes years. some people mistake the length of time for difficulty. but learning is so easy that it would be impossible for you to actually not learn, given enough exposure and experience

item.title: Are there any songs of yours in your catalogue where you didn't write all of the elements as one from the beginning (eg. lyrics)? If so, would you care to share which ones are those?
item.description:
4.30.26 2:47 am
Q: Are there any songs of yours in your catalogue where you didn't write all of the elements as one from the beginning (eg. lyrics)? If so, would you care to share which ones are those?
A: when writing, occasionally the melody/chords will try to get ahead of the lyrics. and as soon as this happens, the whole machine withers to a halt within seconds. however, the words are sometimes allowed to get ahead of the music by maybe a quarter of a second. you think of words and then a quarter of a second later you melodify it with chords etc. Also occasionally a fun exercise is to come up with titles. just a title that sounds cool, without any music. then melodify them later. Also, another way the words can get ahead is when theyre not exact. so for example, if the melody starts to keep getting ahead and everything is drying up, i remind myself to push back into the words realm and just go and brainstorm what i want the next part to talk about. and then i can paraphrase it musically. Also what can happen sometimes is the first idea for a song will be an entire section of melody (usually a chorus, or sometimes first verse). then later the words have to be found, which is usually a very tedious and long search process. so if i may attempt to summarize,...... the melody never gets more than 1 section ahead, and the words never get more than 1 line ahead. and in both of those cases it's almost always exclusively in the case of the first idea. and then generally as the songwriting moves forward, the melody has a tendency to TRY to get ahead, but when it does for more than 1 second it sucks the life out of everything and i have to remind myself to get the words back on board

item.title: I am a new bass player (I started after Christmas of 2025), and have been playing guitar for a full year before that. I want to know this: how do I get better at bass? How do I "slap" the bass like pros do? How do I build up speed?
item.description:
5.7.26 5:07 pm
Q: I am a new bass player (I started after Christmas of 2025), and have been playing guitar for a full year before that. I want to know this: how do I get better at bass? How do I "slap" the bass like pros do? How do I build up speed?
A: to be a bass player is to provide the bass notes in a song where the other higher instruments are taking care of the rest. absolutely vital to a full band song arrangement. and yet, the bass on its own is almost useless. to get the hang of this relationship just takes time and experience doing this, and if you dont have a band youre playing with, you can still play along to recordings any of your favorite songs with the low end turned off on the song. you dont actually even need software or effects to mute the bass on a song, you can just play it through a phone speaker, poof no bass now the bass is you. now see if you can make the music sound full again using your bass. song without bass + you on the bass, equals full song and you being a bass player. that is what the game of bass playing entails. it always amazes me how hard this is to explain, but i think i have explained it

I have an old kiddie piano with two octaves (non configurable) that I COULD use to learn piano, but i feel like I could do better with a higher-grade piano.
